title: Verdier biduality at algebraically closed coefficients
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ and a prime $\ell\neq p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, with structure morphism $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism], and finite type refers to the structure morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each finite intermediate extension $\Ql\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$, use the rationalized category $D^b_c(X,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and its Verdier duality of [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. Use the common-stage category $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the tensor, pullback and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the compact-support and exceptional functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Here internal Hom and the exceptional functors at a finite coefficient field are identified with these coefficient-passage operations by [lem-coef-rational-operations]. A retract means maps $i:P\to K$, $p:K\to P$ with $p\circ i=1_P$.

The finite coefficient-field dualities and their scalar-extension comparisons
induce an exact $\Qlb$-linear anti-equivalence

$$
D_{X,\Qlb}:D^b_c(X,\Qlb)^{\mathrm{op}}
\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,\Qlb),
\qquad (E,K)\longmapsto(E,D_{X,E}K).
$$

It is the internal Hom into $\omega_{X,\Qlb}=Ra_X^!\Qlb$
in the common-stage category. Evaluation and biduality descend,
giving a natural isomorphism
$K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,\Qlb}D_{X,\Qlb}K$.
For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ to a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, the same passage
gives the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ and
$Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$. All of these maps are compatible with
finite scalar extension and with retracts.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ for the rationalized stages used in the statement and $T_{M/E}$ for their scalar extension. Form the pair category from these stages exactly as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. We construct the contravariant functor directly on its representatives. By [thm-coef-rational-verdier], $D_E=D_{W,E}$ is a contravariant exact $E$-linear equivalence, with coherent isomorphisms $b_{M/E,K}:T_{M/E}D_EK\to D_M(T_{M/E}K)$. Define $D(E,K)=(E,D_EK)$ and, for $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L$, put
$$d_M(u)=b_{M/E,K}^{-1}\circ D_M(u)\circ b_{M/F,L}:
T_{M/F}D_FL\longrightarrow T_{M/E}D_EK.$$
This has exactly the source and target required for a representative of $D(F,L)\to D(E,K)$.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: opposite categories and displayed morphism formula

proof.text:
For $M\subseteq N$, denote the scalar associator $T_{N/M}T_{M/H}A\to T_{N/H}A$ by $a_A$. Transport is $u_N=a_L\circ T_{N/M}(u)\circ a_K^{-1}$, where $a_K$ uses $H=E$ and $a_L$ uses $H=F$. The full coherence equation is
$$b_{N/H,A}=D_N(a_A^{-1})\circ b_{N/M,T_{M/H}A}\circ T_{N/M}(b_{M/H,A})\circ a_{D_HA}^{-1}.$$
Here $a_A:T_{N/M}T_{M/H}A\to T_{N/H}A$ and $D_N(a_A^{-1})$ has target $D_N(T_{N/H}A)$. After identifying the iterated extensions through these associators, this reads $b_{N/H}=b_{N/M}\circ T_{N/M}(b_{M/H})$. Contravariant naturality at $u$ is
$$D_N(T_{N/M}u)\circ b_{N/M,T_{M/F}L}
 =b_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}\circ T_{N/M}(D_Mu).$$
Insert these equations into $d_N(u_N)$; the two $b_{N/M}$ factors cancel, leaving
$$d_N(u_N)=a_{D_EK}\circ T_{N/M}(d_M(u))\circ a_{D_FL}^{-1}.$$
Thus this is exactly transport of the dual representative. If two representatives agree at a further field $P$, so do their dual representatives at $P$, which proves representative independence. At one common stage the adjacent inverse comparisons cancel to give $d(vu)=d(u)d(v)$ and $d(1)=1$; additivity follows from additivity of $D_M$. These computations establish the functor laws. For a finite diagram choose representatives for its finitely many objects and arrows, then take the compositum of their fields. For each asserted equality, the representative relation of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] supplies a further finite field where it holds. Taking the compositum of these finitely many witness fields realizes the entire diagram and all its equations at once. No faithfulness of scalar extension is required.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: independence of the common field and of representatives

proof.text: The $\Qlb$-action on a morphism class is computed by choosing a finite stage containing its representative field and the scalar $\alpha$, and multiplying its representative by $\alpha$ there. Such a stage exists because $\alpha$ is algebraic over $\Ql$; changing it does not change the class by the transport computation in step 2. Since $D_M$ is $M$-linear, $d_M(\alpha u)=\alpha d_M(u)$ at that stage, proving $\Qlb$-linearity (there is no conjugation of coefficients). A distinguished triangle is, by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], isomorphic to a finite-stage distinguished triangle. Applying the exact contravariant functor $D_E$ gives a distinguished dual triangle at that field. The image of each arrow is its dual under the formula in step 1, with the scalar comparisons giving the vertex identifications. For the shift comparison use the class of the canonical finite-stage $D_E(K[1])\cong(D_EK)[-1]$. For this check use the tensor and internal-Hom interpretation in [lem-coef-rational-operations]. Write $c:(D_EK)[-1]\otimes K[1]\xrightarrow{\sim}D_EK\otimes K$ for the canonical tensor-shift isomorphism. The inverse shift comparison is the adjoint transpose of $\operatorname{ev}_{E,K}\circ c$. Both ways of comparing its scalar extension with the corresponding map at $M$ transpose to the scalar extension of this displayed composite: the tensor comparisons commute with shifts, and $b$ preserves evaluation by [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. Injectivity of the tensor–Hom adjunction therefore gives equality of the two comparisons, with the signs already specified by $c$. Hence these shift comparisons are natural on common-stage classes. The image of every distinguished triangle is therefore the finite-stage distinguished dual triangle under the specified shift comparison, proving exactness.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: exactness and linearity

proof.text:
Represent evaluation for $(E,K)$ by $\operatorname{ev}_{E,K}$, and represent the bidual map by $\delta_{E,K}:K\to D_E^2K$. Compatibility with scalar extension is part of [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. Explicitly the compatibility identity for the latter is
$$D_M(b_{M/E,K})\circ\delta_{M,T_{M/E}K}
=b_{M/E,D_EK}\circ T_{M/E}(\delta_{E,K}).$$
The sources of both sides are $T_{M/E}K$ and the targets are $D_M(T_{M/E}D_EK)$. This identity and naturality of $\delta_M$ prove naturality of the represented bidual map for $[M,u]$; the analogous evaluation identity proves naturality of evaluation. Define its inverse by $[E,\delta_{E,K}^{-1}]$. The two compositions are identity representatives already at $E$, so the bidual map is an isomorphism. The functor $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasi-inverse of $D:\mathcal C_W^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C_W$: the two composites are double duality on $\mathcal C_W$ and on its opposite, and the isomorphism just constructed (and its opposite/inverse as needed) identifies both composites with the corresponding identity functor. This proves the asserted anti-equivalence without adjoining any new objects.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: evaluation, delta and the finite-stage inverse

proof.text:
Choose the object $\Omega_W=(\Ql,\omega_{W,\Ql})$. The dualizing-object comparisons of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], rationalized in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], identify its representative at every finite stage $E$ with $\omega_{W,E}$; their unit and composition equations make the identification independent of the stage. By [lem-coef-rational-operations], $D_EK=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{W,E})$. Consequently the common-stage internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] sends $((E,K),\Omega_W)$ to an object canonically isomorphic to $(E,D_EK)$. The map on a representative is exactly $d_M(u)$: its two coefficient comparisons are the internal-Hom comparisons from the same integral finite-extension lemma. Thus this is an identification of functors and evaluations. For completeness its internal-Hom property can be read on Hom sets: represent $P,K$ at a common field $M$ and use the finite-stage internal-Hom adjunction supplied by the internal Hom in [lem-coef-rational-operations],
$$\operatorname{Hom}_M(P_M\otimes_M^L K_M,\omega_{W,M})
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_M(P_M,D_MK_M).$$
Its evaluation and transpose respect coefficient extension. Taking representatives gives a map between the two filtered Hom colimits; its inverse is represented by the inverse finite-stage adjunction. Both composites are identities at the representative field, so these are inverse natural bijections on common-stage Hom sets. This proves internal Hom into $\Omega_W$, rather than only an objectwise coincidence.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: tensor–Hom adjunction and identification of internal Hom

proof.text: To apply the strict identity convention of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], normalize the scalar diagram using the canonical tensor unit $T_{E/E}\cong1$ and the identity-compatible tensor associators of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Set the self-transitions and repeated-field associators equal to identities, leaving the strict-inclusion transitions unchanged; transport the functor comparisons through these unit isomorphisms. The unit equations give the repeated-field tower equations, and the remaining tower equations are unchanged. This normalized pair category identifies canonically with the original one: conjugate a representative by the unit isomorphism at either endpoint where its common field equals its field of definition. Naturality of the unit isomorphism makes these conjugations commute with transport, and the adjacent inverse unit isomorphisms cancel in composition. Thus this normalization changes neither the common-stage category nor the descended operation. For each of the covariant families $Rf_{!,E}$ and $Rf_E^!$, the scalar-comparison isomorphisms satisfy the unit, associator, and naturality equations required by [lem-coef-rational-operations]. The coherent pair-functor descent statement [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] therefore gives well-defined functors on common-stage objects and morphisms, and gives the descended compatible natural transformations. On objects the left functor is $(E,K)\mapsto(E,Rf_{!,E}K)$, exactly the common-stage compact-support operation of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: exceptional adjunction and its units and counits

proof.text:
For $K=(E,K_E)$ and $L=(F,L_F)$, index by the finite fields $M\supseteq E,F$. Set
$$A_M=\operatorname{Hom}_{Y,M}(Rf_{!,M}T_{M/E}K_E,T_{M/F}L_F),\quad B_M=\operatorname{Hom}_{X,M}(T_{M/E}K_E,Rf_M^!T_{M/F}L_F).$$
Use the scalar comparisons from step 6 in their transition maps. The representative prescription of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] identifies their direct limits with $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!K,L)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Rf^!L)$ respectively. The adjunction in [lem-coef-rational-operations] gives $e_M:A_M\cong B_M$. Its formulas are $e_M(u)=Rf_M^!(u)\circ\eta$ and $e_M^{-1}(v)=\epsilon\circ Rf_{!,M}(v)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. These are additive, since the functors are additive. Preservation of unit and counit under coefficient extension gives precisely $e_Nu_{MN}=v_{MN}e_M$. Apply [lem-coef-qbar-adjunction-hom-descent] to obtain inverse bijections of the two common-stage Hom groups. Naturality in $K,L$ is checked on representatives: put a precomposition or postcomposition and the argument over one finite field, where it is the naturality identity of the finite-stage adjunction. Thus the bijections are natural in both variables.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: exceptional adjunction and its units and counits

proof.text: The descended Hom bijections are natural in both variables. Applying the natural-bijection adjunction construction [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] supplies the unit and counit and proves both triangle identities; their finite-stage components are the given units and counits. Hence the descended functors form the constructible adjunction.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: exceptional adjunction and its units and counits

proof.text: The natural finite-stage isomorphism $Rf_E^!\cong D_{X,E}f_E^*D_{Y,E}$ of [lem-coef-rational-operations] preserves evaluations, units and counits under finite scalar extension. Pullback has its coherent scalar comparisons from [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], rationalized by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; duality has those of [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. Hence the composite on the right is the descended $D_Xf^*D_Y$, and the finite-stage isomorphism and its inverse define inverse natural transformations to it from the right adjoint of step 6. This is precisely the common-stage exceptional operation of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], since it has the same coefficient-passage representatives and the same adjunction maps. Taking $f=a_X$ and applying [lem-coef-rational-operations] to the coefficient unit gives $Ra_X^!\Qlb=(\Ql,Ra_{X,\Ql}^!\Ql)=(\Ql,\omega_{X,\Ql})=\Omega_X$ under the canonical identifications. This identifies the object used in step 5 with the dualizing object asserted in the statement. All finite scalar-extension compatibilities hold as represented equations; their unit and composition equations therefore remain true in the common-stage category.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph: identification of omega and Rf^!, and coefficient compatibility

proof.text:
Let $i:P\to K$, $p:K\to P$ be a retract, so $pi=1_P$. By the finite-field and equality-witness construction in step 2, applied to [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], enlarge to a finite stage representing $P,K,i,p$ and this equality. There $D(p):DP\to DK$ and $D(i):DK\to DP$ satisfy $D(i)D(p)=1_{DP}$, and the restricted evaluation is
$$DP\otimes P\xrightarrow{D(p)\otimes i}DK\otimes K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K}\omega.$$
Naturality of evaluation identifies this composite with $\operatorname{ev}_P\circ(1_{DP}\otimes pi)=\operatorname{ev}_P$. Naturality of biduality gives
$$D^2(p)\circ\delta_K\circ i=\delta_P\circ pi=\delta_P,$$
and its inverse is $p\circ\delta_K^{-1}\circ D^2(i)$, by naturality of $\delta^{-1}$ and $pi=1$. The evaluation and biduality compatibility with split idempotents and with finite scalar extension is also stated in [lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation]; its pairing clause applies to the adjoint idempotents $ip$ on $K$ and $D(ip)$ on $DK$. For the other descended natural maps, restriction is simply naturality: if $\eta:F\to G$, then $G(p)\eta_KF(i)=\eta_PF(p)F(i)=\eta_P$. For contravariant $F,G$, the restriction equation is instead
$$G(i)\circ\eta_K\circ F(p)=\eta_P\circ F(i)\circ F(p)=\eta_P\circ F(pi)=\eta_P.$$
For a transformation of several variables apply the respective displayed equation to each variable, holding the others fixed. An inverse natural isomorphism restricts too, and its two inverse equations remain identities of the summand. Apply these equations to the adjunction identifications, evaluations and biduality already constructed. They hold at the common finite stage and hence on classes. This proves every asserted retract compatibility; it makes no identification with an ambient derived category obtained by tensoring with an infinite topological coefficient extension.
